Hi Alice / team — thanks for looping us in. Quick summary of Redwood's vulnerability management and sharing policy to help your security review: 

- Pen test reporting: We can provide a redacted executive summary of the most recent third-party pen test (redwood-pen-test-summary-2025.pdf). For full reports, we require an approved NDA and we typically share via secure link (SecureLabs or S3 with short-lived tokens).

- Scanning cadence: internal authenticated scans weekly, external/full-scope scans quarterly, and continuous SCA for dependencies.

- SLA & remediation targets:
  - Critical: acknowledge within 4 business hours, remediation plan within 72 hours
  - High: acknowledge within 24 hours, remediation plan within 7 days
  - Medium/Low: triage and roadmap within 30 days

- Disclosure & external vendor coordination: we have a coordinated disclosure policy — we notify customers for findings that affect customer data and publish anonymized CVE timelines for issues discovered in open-source dependencies. We coordinate with vendors (e.g., SecureLabs) to ensure redaction and handling of sensitive test artifacts.

- Evidence & compliance: we can share SOC 2 Type II summary (control scope and status) and a high-level vulnerability management policy (vuln-management-policy.pdf). For GDPR data flow concerns, we provide DPA language and can add specific clarifications for the pilot if needed.

Attachments: redwood-pen-test-summary-2025.pdf, vuln-management-policy.pdf, soc2-type2-summary.pdf (redacted)

If SecureLabs needs a point of contact to exchange the full report after NDA, please have them reach out to security@redwood.com and we'll set up a secure transfer.
